Finally, we infer bolometric luminosities for the sample and construct a bolometric luminosity function. We integrate over this luminosity function to derive a black hole accretion density (BHAD) of $4.8^{+5.8}_{-2.6}\times10^{-7}~M_{\odot}~\textrm{yr}^{-1}~\textrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, showing broad agreement with previous photometric work, but disagreement with previous X-ray models, reinforcing the idea that BLAGN are more common in the early universe than previously expected.

2610.36752.title: Relativistic N-body simulations with mass-varying neutrinos
2610.36752.abstract: Recent cosmological data provide weak hints for smaller masses than what is required by neutrino-oscillation experiments, motivating investigations into variation of the neutrino masses with cosmic time. Here we study a model where the neutrinos couple to a quintessence field that acts as dark energy. We compute structure formation using fully dynamical and relativistic N-body and lattice simulations, with nonlinear field evolution and a weak-field metric expansion. Similar to previous studies, we find the generic appearance of neutrino lumps, but observe them to be highly dynamical and spinning. We study several models where the effective dark energy, including nonlinear effects of the scalar field on the cosmic expansion, can show phantom crossing. The relativistic physics available in our simulation framework can help distinguish such models from LCDM, through observations of neutrino and dark energy properties, and slip between the gravitational potentials due to anisotropic stress. The rich phenomenology offered by mass-varying neutrinos motivates further exploration and development of the simulation techniques.

2610.38673.title: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows
2610.38673.abstract: Black hole (BH) spin grows as accretion supplies angular momentum and decreases as magnetically driven jets remove it, driving the BH toward an equilibrium spin, $a_{\rm \star; eq}$. Existing estimates of $a_{\rm \star; eq}$ rely on general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations with fixed BH mass and spin, and cover only the extreme limits of horizon magnetic flux $φ\rightarrow0$ and magnetically arrested disks (MADs), $φ\approxφ_{\rm MAD}$. We evolve the BH mass and spin in long 3D GRMHD simulations of radiatively inefficient accretion flows aligned or anti-aligned with the BH spin. We find the spin-up parameter as a function of BH spin and $φ/φ_{\rm MAD}$, and derive the equilibrium spin as a continuous function of flux, $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD})$. The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm \star; eq}\approx0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx0.5$ to $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx0.06$ in sustained MADs. In weakly magnetized flows, a slowly spinning BH must accrete at least its initial mass to reach equilibrium, whereas MADs spin down rapidly rotating BHs after accreting less than half of it. However, as the BH grows, the growing gravitational radius and enhanced inflow reduce $φ/φ_{\rm MAD}$, driving disks whose magnetic-flux supply cannot keep pace out of the MAD state and allowing the BH to transition from spin-down to spin-up. The final spin thus depends on both the magnetic flux history and the accreted mass. We discuss implications for a variety of BH-powered engines and provide a subgrid prescription for galaxy-scale simulations and population studies.

2610.37971.title: The Carousel Lens III: Joint lens convergence and source kinematic modeling
2610.37971.abstract: We introduce a new, independent modeling component to the Carousel Lens series by exploiting the spatially-resolved kinematics contained within the lensed arcs, which so far has remained rather underexplored in strong-lensing analyses. We present an end-to-end forward-modeling framework that reconstructs an integral-field spectroscopic datacube from a parameterization of the lens convergence profile together with the line-of-sight velocity, velocity dispersion, and surface brightness profiles of the unlensed source. The kinematic structure of the source acts as an additional set of ray-traceable markers distributed across every lensed image, inaccessible from imaging data alone. Furthermore, by generating an [OII] emission-line datacube, we isolate a single source redshift and remove lens and line-of-sight light contamination. We apply this framework to deep VLT/MUSE observations of the Carousel Lens, modeling the [OII] emission of the quadruply-imaged star-forming galaxy at $z_{\rm s} = 1.432$ that anchors the system's cosmography constraints. We measure an Einstein radius $θ_{\rm E} = 12.816''^{+0.005}_{-0.007}$ and a logarithmic slope $γ= 1.412^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, tightening the statistical uncertainties on both by roughly a factor of $2-2.5$ relative to the corresponding flat emission-line map model. We find that the source galaxy exhibits a strong rotation, lies confidently along the star-forming main sequence, and has an inferred central black hole mass of $\log M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot} = 7.89 \pm 0.51$. These results establish datacube-level forward modeling as a practical and independent route to traditional image-based lens models in the current systematics-limited regime, and one that extends naturally to this system's other lensed sources and to other lens systems.

2610.37782.title: The Redshift-Space Cluster-Galaxy Cross-Correlation as a Probe of Gravity on Cosmic Scales
2610.37782.abstract: Testing General Relativity (GR) on cosmological scales requires probes that are directly sensitive to gravitational dynamics. We present a Fisher matrix forecast of how well the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) can constrain departures from GR through the cluster infall velocity field, using the redshift-space cluster-galaxy cross-correlation function $ξ^{\rm s}_{\rm cg}(r_p, r_π)$ as the primary observable. We construct mock catalogs from the AbacusSummit N-body simulations, using a Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) model for galaxies and a log-normal mass-observable relation for cluster selection. We parameterize departures from GR with a single multiplicative factor $F_{\rm G}$ that rescales halo infall velocities relative to the GR prediction. Marginalizing over the HOD, mass-observable, and cosmological parameters, we find that DESI BGS can constrain $F_{\rm G}$ to $σ(F_{\rm G}) = 0.033$ at $z \sim 0.3$. This precision is sufficient to distinguish representative $f(R)$ and Galileon gravity models from GR at $\gtrsim 4σ$. The strongest limitation is a degeneracy between $F_{\rm G}$ and the scatter in the cluster mass-observable relation, while the constraint shows no strong degeneracy with any individual HOD parameter. Perfect knowledge of the galaxy-halo connection would improve the constraint to $σ(F_{\rm G}) \approx 0.015$, and including the galaxy autocorrelation function in the data vector could recover part of this improvement. The same data vector yields tight constraints on the cosmological parameters, $σ(Ω_m) = 0.010$ and $σ(σ_8) = 0.010$, only moderately correlated with $F_{\rm G}$. These results demonstrate the potential of DESI BGS cluster-galaxy correlations to test gravity on quasi-linear scales, complementary to existing modified gravity probes and to weak-lensing cluster mass profiles.

2610.38083.title: The scale of homogeneity in DESI Data Release 1
2610.38083.abstract: We present measurements of the scale of cosmic homogeneity using the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), the largest publicly available spectroscopic extragalactic survey to date. Using a counts-in-spheres estimator applied to nearly 5 million galaxies and quasars across six independent redshift bins spanning $0.1 < z < 2.1$, we measure the correlation dimension $D_2(r)$ and define the homogeneity scale $R_H$ as the point at which the galaxy distribution reaches within 1\% of the homogeneous asymptotic value. We find that all tracers clearly transition to homogeneity, with the galaxy homogeneity scale ranging from $93.8^{+0.9}_{-0.7}$ to $142.6^{+1.4}_{-1.4}$ $h^{-1}$Mpc depending on the tracer redshift, galaxy bias, and modelling used to extract the scale. Using a cosmology-dependent model, we reconstruct the underlying matter homogeneity scale, finding it decreases monotonically with redshift in excellent agreement with $Λ$CDM predictions. We identify a systematic offset of up to $\sim 10\%$ between measurements in the North and South Galactic Caps, largely due to fiber assignment effects reproduced in our simulations. Accounting for this, and with a complementary demonstration using toy models that our methodology correctly identifies inhomogeneous universes in all but rather finely-tuned observer configurations, this hence provides strong evidence in favour of the cosmological principle across our full redshift range. Our matter homogeneity scale measurements are consistent with, and substantially more precise than, previous constraints from WiggleZ and SDSS, demonstrating the power of DESI data for precision tests of the cosmological principle.

2610.38607.title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
2610.38607.abstract: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four major spiral arms, including the Norma-Outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the "Norma arm" extending from one end of the Galaxy's central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. We now use a new generation of N-body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year old masers instead trace the Galactic bar's Quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust-lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the bar's parameters to be: a ~ 4.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, b ~ 2.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, phi = 20 (+5/-2) deg, Omega_p <~ 40 km s^-1 kpc^-1, representing the bar's semi-major and semi-minor half-lengths, inclination angle and pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way's spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

2610.38540.title: Understanding the origin of silver in metal-poor stars based on the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium analysis of Ag I lines
2610.38540.abstract: Silver is a poorly observed neutron-capture element, and understanding its Galactic production history requires accurate abundances for stellar samples covering a broad metallicity range. We refined the method for calculating stellar Ag abundances by considering the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) line formation for Ag I. A comprehensive model atom of silver was built from the atomic data available in the literature, including recent data on inelastic Ag I + H I collisions. We derived abundances using the high-resolution spectra and the synthetic spectrum method with the one-dimensional model atmospheres. From two Ag I lines in the solar spectrum we obtained the NLTE abundances log epsilon = 1.15 and 1.10 for different treatments of collisions with hydrogen atoms. The NLTE abundances of Ag were determined for the first time for 41 stars in the -2.74 <= [Fe/H] <= -0.56 metallicity range. The NLTE abundance corrections for Ag I 3382 A were found to be larger for the giants (up to 0.92~dex) than the dwarfs (up to 0.51~dex). In NLTE, Ag in our sample stars is enhanced relatively to Fe and the [Ag/Fe] Galactic trend is very similar to that for [Eu/Fe]; the [Ag/Eu], [Ag/Ba], and [Ag/Sr] abundance ratios of the r-II stars CS22892-052 and CS31082-001 agree very well with the r-process model of Prantzos et al. (2020); the -1.6 < [Fe/H] <= -0.56 stars have close-to-solar [Ag/Eu] ratios. We conclude that production of silver was dominated by the main r-process throughout the metallicity range we investigated, with the main s-process contribution of not larger than 20% for [Fe/H] > -1.6.

2610.38848.title: SuperCrude EoS: A Simple, Analytical, and Reasonably Accurate Equation of State for Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics
2610.38848.abstract: We present SuperCrude, a vastly simplified astrophysical equation of state that captures the most important physics needed for explosive astrophysics, but using compact, physically-motivated analytical approximations rather than precise interpolated data tables. We present a number of code tests demonstrating the performance of SuperCrude in a wide range of parameter space. In large regions of parameter space, SuperCrude is precisely accurate to within the accuracy level of helmeos. For some regions (especially where degeneracy, gas, and radiation are comparable) SuperCrude has errors in its effective adiabatic index on the order of a few percent. The solver's estimate of the temperature is less accurate, on the order of tens of percent. Because the solver is analytic, SuperCrude is designed in such a way to guarantee exact thermodynamic consistency. We incorporate SuperCrude into some hydrodynamic and astrophysical test problems, including the thermonuclear explosion of a white dwarf star. When coupled with a stiff nuclear network, SuperCrude does not achieve the same nucleosynthetic yields as helmeos, motivating future work to improve the temperature accuracy further.

2610.37646.title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
2610.37646.abstract: Magnetic fields are vital in determining the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos. They are, however, notoriously difficult to observe. This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences. Although Faraday rotation measures (RMs) offer a direct probe of magnetic fields, it weights magnetic fields by the free-electron density. Several probes of free electrons, including fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) and kinematic SZ (kSZ) effect, are now maturing into precision tools. We combine RM$^2$ stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical depth profiles constrained jointly by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect, and obtain 95% upper limits on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field of $<3.9$-$11.6~μ$G ($<2.3$-$6.4~μ$G) in groups (clusters) for a 10~kpc coherence length. Combining these with thermal pressure profiles inferred from tSZ-shear cross-correlations, we obtain 95% lower limits on the plasma $β$ of $>0.31$ ($>11$) in groups (clusters). Although current constraints are only limits, we forecast a first detection with larger datasets from the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA). We present the first forecast of the DSA RM grid density ($\sim365$ RMs deg$^{-2}$), which when combined with 10$^4$ FRBs would measure the field in groups to $3$-$13\%$ precision, compared to current constraints of $38$-$75\%$. Although the interpretation of current measurements remains challenging owing to depolarization along turbulent halo sightlines and the unknown coherence length, larger samples and DSA/Square Kilometer Array observations may resolve these uncertainties by measuring polarization-fraction profiles and the RM structure function using extended radio sources, respectively.

2610.38633.title: Kinematic methods of spiral nature identification: limitations and applicability
2610.38633.abstract: The nature of spiral arms in galaxies remains debated, with several competing formation scenarios, including density waves, kinematic spirals, dynamic spirals, and recurrent modes, that are difficult to distinguish observationally. We tested two kinematic methods - the phase reversal method and the velocity harmonic dominance method - using toy models and mock data from TNG50 simulations. For bar resonances, the phase reversal method is strongly orientation-dependent and yields reliable corotation estimates only when the bar is aligned with the disc minor axis. For spiral arms, the phase reversal method does not always yield reliable results and should be used in tondem with another kinematic method. The velocity harmonic dominance method is more robust: it distinguishes between density wave, kinematic, and dynamic spiral patterns, although it still shows some sensitivity to orientation. Uncertainties in the rotation curve do not strongly affect its results. We also apply both methods to the observed grand-design spiral galaxy NGC3938 as an illustrative example; the results suggest the presence of multiple spiral modes, consistent with the recurrent modes scenario and this interpretation relies on different indirect evidence. Based on our findings, we propose a strategy for classifying spiral structure in observed galaxies that combines multiple independent tests. Applying this analysis to an extended sample will allow us to validate its predictive power and to investigate the diversity of spiral formation scenarios.

2610.38811.title: The extragalactic science of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen spectroscopic survey II: Discovery of a galaxy cluster at z = 0.089 behind the Galactic plane
2610.38811.abstract: The Zone of Avoidance (ZoA) continues to represent the most significant incompleteness in the extragalactic census of the Local Universe. It is evident that photometric surveys alone are insufficient to establish whether the galaxy overdensities detected therein are physical systems or projections along the line of sight. We present the first spectroscopic results of the extragalactic science area of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, demonstrating how near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy can reveal and dynamically characterise galaxy clusters hidden by the Milky Way. A photometric overdensity of 19 galaxy candidates was identified in the VVV NIRGC III catalogue, centred at $(l,b)=(274.05^\circ,+2.85^\circ)$ with a mean interstellar extinction of $A_{K_s}=0.2$ mag; 16 of these candidates were observed with VLT/KMOS in the $HK$ grating and yielded spectra with reliable cross-correlation radial velocities. A total of 14 galaxies form a compact structure with a mean redshift of $\langle z \rangle = 0.089 \pm 0.001$, which corresponds to a mean radial velocity $\langle cz \rangle = 26660 \pm 170$ km/s, while two are foreground galaxies. The rest-frame line-of-sight velocity dispersion is $σ_v = 560^{+110}_{-120}$ km/s, implying an indicative dynamical mass of $M_{200} = 1.9^{+0.7}_{-1.1} \times 10^{14} M_\odot$ (based on members within the cluster core $\sim 0.4 r_{200}$) and placing the system in the poor-cluster regime. Of these 14 cluster members, 13 also lie within the $2σ$ scatter of the fitted near-IR red sequence. The other two galaxies are foreground objects that lie outside this range.

2610.38886.title: Odds Estimation for Supermassive Black Hole Binaries in Local Core Galaxies
2610.38886.abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) are expected products of massive galaxy mergers, but identifying binaries in nearby galaxies remains challenging. We combine simulated massive-galaxy assembly histories from IllustrisTNG with a semi-analytic core-scouring model to connect observable core galaxy properties to the probability of hosting a bound SMBHB at z=0. We (i) construct a core galaxy population using an observationally motivated galaxy stellar mass function, (ii) model binary evolution through dynamical friction, stellar hardening, and gravitational-wave emission, and (iii) perform logistic regressions with five observable predictors: stellar mass deficit, stellar mass, central density, central velocity dispersion, and effective radius. The resulting models perform well on simulated systems, achieving a pseudo-$R^2$ of $0.51\pm0.03$, accuracy $0.95\pm0.01$, precision $0.92\pm0.03$, and recall $0.82\pm0.04$. Uncoalesced binaries are typically compact, with separations peaking near 0.3 pc, though only $\sim0.3\%$ emit in the pulsar timing array band. Applying the model to observed core galaxies, we identify eight nearby galaxies more likely than not to host SMBHBs. Of those eight host candidates, we note Messier 86 (NGC 4406) as a particularly likely example that was similarly identified using independent means and therefore warrants future follow-up.

2610.36543.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Differential Calibration of the Gaia DR3 Parallax Zero Point Using Galactic Globular Clusters
2610.36543.abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) occupy a broad range of stellar colors and magnitudes while sharing nearly the same distance. Gaia Data Release 3 parallaxes retain systematic zero-point residual variations for GCs, even after the correction by the widely used standard correction model (L21). We derive an empirical residual correction by the Hierarchical Bayesian Model, separating cluster-level offsets from the differential information carried by the member sequences. We first evaluate the L21 baseline at a fixed reference color, which assigns the remaining color-dependent correction to the residual model. Then we model the residual zero point, $δZ(G,ν_{\rm eff})$, with B-splines functions in color and magnitude--color interaction terms. The uncorrected cluster residuals exhibit a negative offset of approximately $25$--$40~μ{\rm as}$. The L21 baseline removes most of this offset but leaves coherent color- and magnitude-dependent structure. Applying the residual model brings the mean residuals close to zero, especially across most of the sampled color range. In five-fold cross-validation that excludes entire clusters from training, the correction modestly reduces the magnitude- and color-trend RMS relative to the L21 correction. The resulting model therefore provides a differential refinement of the \textit{Gaia} DR3 parallax zero-point within the calibrated domain for GCs, rather than an independent determination of its absolute value.

2610.37574.title: Effects of Dust in Electron-Capture Supernovae: Difficulty in Explaining Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients
2610.37574.abstract: The progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs) spanning the luminosity gap between novae and supernovae are under debate, and electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) have been proposed as a strong candidate. ECSNe from super asymptotic giant branch (super-AGB) stars have been theoretically predicted to be much brighter than ILRTs, but attenuation by dusty winds of their super-AGB progenitors may ease this tension. Here we construct a semi-analytical framework for calculating the light curves of ECSNe with dust attenuation and re-emission, by combining recent ECSN light curve predictions with a model for dust physics. Even by varying both the wind mass-loss rate and the ECSN model parameters, we find it challenging to simultaneously fit the light curve and color evolution of ILRTs. This poses a potential challenge to the standard models of ECSNe for explaining ILRTs. For explaining ILRTs, we propose either the existence of a population of ECSNe with much lower explosion energies ($\sim$10$^{48}$-$10^{49}$ erg) and dimmer plateaus, or alternative model(s) to ECSNe that realize such low explosion energies.

2610.38733.title: Towards constraining cosmology with HI--galaxy cross-correlations from MeerKLASS
2610.38733.abstract: We present an inference of cosmological parameters from the cross-correlation power spectrum between the MeerKLASS 2019 L-band HI intensity maps and the overlapping WiggleZ galaxies at $z \simeq 0.43$. The analysis is intended as a proof of concept to verify that the full pipeline, from the foreground cleaning of the maps to the likelihood analysis, can be applied end-to-end to real data and can return results consistent with the concordance cosmology. The model of the observed power spectrum includes observational effects that are relevant to a single-dish experiment. In the most optimistic scenario in which we hold the astrophysical nuisance parameters fixed, we obtain $H_0 = 65.3^{+5.8}_{-10}\text{ km s}^{-1}\text{ Mpc}^{-1}$ and $Ω_{\text{m}} = 0.44^{+0.12}_{-0.30}$ at the 68% confidence level. We find that sampling the HI amplitude with an informative prior retains most of the constraining power and changes these results by less than 1 sigma. Moreover, using synthetic data, we show that neglecting the observational effects in the model biases the inferred parameters by up to 2.5 sigma and also underestimates their uncertainties. Finally, we show that varying the number of foreground modes removed and the range of scales included changes the inferred parameters by less than 0.5 sigma. These results demonstrate the robustness of our pipeline in modelling HI intensity mapping data, and set the foundation for future cosmological inference with intensity mapping using MeerKLASS and SKAO.

2610.37775.title: Ejected and Rejected: Strong Scatterings in Dense Star Clusters
2610.37775.abstract: Understanding the evolution of collisional stellar systems is key to predicting both the bulk evolution of dense star clusters and also the rates of tidal disruption events, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar ejections, and other loss cone phenomena. Although a majority of the evolution is dictated by weak, small-angle scatterings, rare close encounters resulting in strong scatterings can sometimes produce qualitatively different outcomes. To systematically determine the astrophysical importance of strong scatterings, we derive the exact differential rate distribution of velocity kicks in isotropic and spherically symmetric distribution functions representing globular and nuclear star clusters, while also deriving the distribution boundaries and approximate rate scalings. We then extend this formalism to derive approximate rates of energy and angular momentum kicks for objects in the nuclear star cluster, and then apply this framework to study (i) ejections and (ii) ``cancellation'' of extreme mass ratio inspirals. We find that ejection rates are complicated in some regimes due to the saturation of the strong kick distribution and the breakdown of the weak limit, likely enhancing the effect of loss cone shielding. We also determine that a sizable fraction of proto-EMRIs will likely be canceled by strong scatterings, highlighting the need for future work to determine to what degree strong scatterings impact the true EMRI rate.

2610.37455.title: Getting Ready For Analysing Rubin Data : CLMM v2, The Updated LSST-DESC Cluster Weak Lensing Mass Modeling Library For Cosmology
2610.37455.abstract: The Dark Energy Science Collaboration has prepared a multitude of pipelines to process the upcoming Vera C. Rubin Observatory data and perform different scientific analyses. Here, we present the methodology to constrain the mass information of galaxy clusters from weak lensing, which is encompassed by the v2.0 release of the Cluster Lensing Mass Modeling (CLMM) code. This Python library provides the ingredients for both the modeling and data reduction of lensing observables, and the improvements in the new version were customized to handle the first WL analyses of LSST clusters, including, e.g., stacking functionalities and WL multipoles. This new version of CLMM has allowed various cluster analyses using LSST-DESC simulated data, precursor survey and Rubin commissioning and survey validation data, and is ready to be used for the first cluster cosmology analyses. CLMM is an open-source software package collaboratively written in Python, providing multiple example notebooks, including a set that can reproduce all figures in this work, and extensive documentation, publicly available at https://lsstdesc.org/CLMM/.

2610.36512.title: ASKAP Discovery of a Giant Odd Radio Circle at $z=0.15$
2610.36512.abstract: Odd radio circles (ORCs) are a recently recognized class of faint, roughly circular diffuse radio sources, typically a few hundred kiloparsecs across, whose origin is still debated. We report the serendipitous discovery of a giant ORC, ORC~J1928$-$5056, in 856~MHz continuum data from the ASKAP observations. The emission forms a single, mildly elliptical structure $4^{\prime}$ across, corresponding to $0.63$~Mpc at the redshift $z=0.1507$ of the central galaxy LEDA~140850, the brightest cluster galaxy of Abell~3639, which makes it one of the largest single ORCs known. After subtracting the radio nucleus associated with the host galaxy, the ORC has a flux density of 73~mJy integrated within an area of $\sim 12$~arcmin$^2$, i.e.\ a mean surface brightness of only $1.7$~$μ$Jy~arcsec$^{-2}$, and a rest-frame luminosity of $L_{1.4}=2\times10^{24}$~W~Hz$^{-1}$, comparable to those of the most luminous ORCs. Including its nucleus, the system reaches $L_{1.4}=6.6\times10^{24}$~W~Hz$^{-1}$, higher than that of any other ORC reported so far. The host is a massive ($M_{\ast}\sim10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$), passive elliptical galaxy with negligible star formation. It contains an AGN jet with a power-law spectrum of index $α=-0.877\pm0.089$ between 856 and 1656~MHz. Finally, we discuss the implications for ORC formation models and the observations needed to establish the nature of this system.

2610.38235.title: Age-Resolved Vertical Motions in the Milky Way Warp: A Localized Enhancement in Intermediate-Age Populations
2610.38235.abstract: Determining how the Milky Way warp evolves provides constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of galactic disks. Using Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment Data Release 19 (APOGEE DR19) spectroscopy, we estimate ages for 222,355 red giants. With Gaia astrometry and geometric distances, we analyze 168,824 of these stars in five age bins spanning $0$--$10$ Gyr. The warp-related radial vertical-velocity ($V_Z$) profile of young red giants ($0$--$2$ Gyr) is broadly consistent with those of classical Cepheids and young open clusters. Over $9\leq R<12$ kpc, we find that the mean $V_Z$ values of the intermediate-age red giants ($2$--$4$ and $4$--$6$ Gyr) are $1.48\pm0.46$ and $1.49\pm0.52$ km s$^{-1}$ higher than that of the young population, respectively. By contrast, at $R\simeq12$--$13$ kpc, the $V_Z$ profiles of the $0$--$6$ Gyr red giants are consistent within their uncertainties. The intermediate-age enhancement persists across our robustness tests and may reflect smaller effective kinematic warp onset radii for the intermediate-age populations. The observed velocity differences may arise from the combined effects of earlier perturbations and the present-day warp, or from differences in vertical structure among stellar populations.

2610.38827.title: The Bochum Survey of the Southern Galactic Disk: IV. Multi-Band Photometry
2610.38827.abstract: The Southern Galactic Disk Survey (GDS) monitored a mosaic of 268 fields along a $6^\circ$-wide stripe in the southern galactic disk from September 2010 to September 2019. These fields were observed between 21 and 407 times simultaneously in $r'$ ($8\,\mathrm{mag} \lesssim r' \lesssim 18\,\mathrm{mag}$) and $i'$ ($7\,\mathrm{mag} \lesssim i' \lesssim 17\,\mathrm{mag}$), supplemented by between 2 and 147 observations in each of the bands $U$, $B$, $V$, and $z'$. Here we present the matched multi-band catalogue, which integrates photometry and light curve data from all bands, containing photometry for almost 21.7 million Gaia DR3 sources, of which $113\,449$ are identified as variables. We give an overview of the survey's variable content with respect to its main characteristics and known variability type classifications. The comparison with the cross-match catalogue of Gaia DR3 sources with variables from the literature compiled by Gavras et al. (2023) and the International Variable Star Index (VSX) indicates that approximately $40\,\%$ of the variable sources remain unclassified in terms of variability type. Light curves for all of these sources are contained in the GDS data catalogues, available via the German Astrophysical Virtual Observatory (GAVO), and can contribute to their classification.

2610.38798.title: Rotation and outburst-like brightenings in ZZ Ceti stars observed by TESS
2610.38798.abstract: Context. Pulsating white dwarfs, such as ZZ Ceti stars, allow for the study of white dwarf rotation through rotationally split pulsation modes. Space-based photometry has also revealed outbursts in some cool ZZ Ceti stars. Aims. We extend the search for rotationally split pulsation multiplets and outburst-like brightenings among known ZZ Ceti stars observed by TESS. We check whether the TESS data add new evidence for a connection between outburst activity and stellar rotation. Methods. We analysed 120 s and 20 s cadence TESS light curves available up to Sector 96. After light curve correction and quality filtering, we performed iterative frequency analysis. Candidate rotationally split multiplets were identified automatically and visually validated. Outburst candidates were selected from smoothed flux excursions, followed by light curve inspection and pixel-level TESS diagnostics. Results. We identify 11 ZZ Ceti stars with accepted triplet candidates and derive rotation periods of about 8-94 h; three triplet detections are reported here for the first time. The targets are broadly consistent with the dispersion of rotation periods found in previous studies. The time-domain search produced 19 outburst-like events in 11 stars after light curve inspection. Pixel-level diagnostics indicate that most are likely caused by foreground asteroid contamination. We identify three stars (TIC 219442838, TIC 307908863, and TIC 630426257) as candidate stellar outbursters. None belong to the accepted triplet-rotation sample.

2610.36573.title: A Collimated Protostellar Outflow Likely Driven by Jet and Reshaped by Environment in the Sagittarius C Cloud of the Central Molecular Zone
2610.36573.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) at the center of the Galaxy provides a nearby laboratory for studying star formation under extreme physical and chemical conditions. Recent ALMA (Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array) observations have identified 43 candidate protostellar outflows in three CMZ clouds. One of these, the Sgr C-F#2 outflow in Sagittarius C (Sgr C), has a highly collimated lobe extending approximately 0.8 pc in projection. Here we present a joint analysis of ALMA observations of SiO J=8-7, 5-4, and 2-1. We use local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods to constrain the SiO column densities, H2 number density, and gas temperature. The low SiO rotational temperatures and higher kinetic temperatures inferred from non-LTE methods suggest subthermal excitation. The elongated SiO morphology, shock-excited gas, position-velocity structure, and the alignment of the red shifted molecular lobe with JWST infrared knots altogether favor jet-dominated entrainment, whereas a broader disk-wind component close to the source cannot be excluded. The outflow shows asymmetries in its morphology and physical properties, which can be attributed to dense gas on the path of its lobe impeding its propagation and feedback from a nearby HII region imposing different pressure on its two sides.

2610.36897.title: Topological Centrality in Gaia Open Clusters
2610.36897.abstract: Open clusters exhibit diverse spatial structures that provide insight into their formation and dynamical evolution. We investigate the relationship between stellar mass segregation, network topology, and dynamical age in 871 dynamically unevolved open clusters ($τ= t/t_{\rm rh} \leq 1$) from Gaia-based catalogs. We construct three-dimensional k-nearest-neighbor graphs and measure Degree Centrality (DC), Closeness Centrality (CL), and Betweenness Centrality (BC). For each measure, we define a network-based mass segregation ratio (MSR) by comparing the mean centrality of the most massive stars with that of all cluster members. We test the stability of these measures across connectivity parameters $k=5$--20 and compare them with the classical 3D MSR, $Λ_{\rm MSR,3D}$, and dynamical age. All three network ratios show positive correlations with $Λ_{\rm MSR,3D}$, strongest for closeness centrality, while their correlations with dynamical age are weak. These results demonstrate that network analysis provides a complementary approach to studying stellar structure and mass segregation in open clusters.

2610.37501.title: Quasinormal Ringing of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by a King Dark Matter Halo: Higher-Order WKB Analysis
2610.37501.abstract: We study scalar and electromagnetic perturbations of a Schwarzschild black hole (BH) surrounded by a dark matter halo described by the King density profile. The lapse function can be expressed as $1-2[M+M_{\rm DM}(r)]/r$, where $M_{\rm DM}(r)$ is the halo mass enclosed within radius $r$; thus, the halo affects the geometry through its enclosed-mass function. We compute the quasinormal frequencies using the sixth-order WKB method and its Padé-improved version. Rewriting the lapse function in terms of the inverse hyperbolic sine avoids the severe numerical cancellations that arise when evaluating its high-order derivatives. For the configurations examined, the fundamental frequencies agree with those extracted from time-domain evolution to within $0.2\%$.The halo lowers both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate. The change of the real part is almost entirely accounted for by the halo mass enclosed by the photon sphere, and the additional decrease of the damping rate follows the ratio of the Lyapunov exponent to the angular frequency of the circular null orbit. Since part of the halo lies inside the horizon in this metric, we also place the halo outside the BH by means of an Einstein cluster. The frequencies then decrease by a similar amount, but the real part follows the Schwarzschild value multiplied by the gravitational redshift factor of the halo. A jump in the density at the inner edge of the halo scatters the waves and changes the damping rate by up to about $9\%$. For a continuous density profile, deviations from the redshift relation remain below about $1.5\%$ for $r_{\rm in}=3M$ and below about $0.5\%$ for the cases with $r_{\rm in}\geq4M$. No unstable modes are found within the perturbation sectors and parameter configurations examined.

2610.38531.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
2610.38531.abstract: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $χ$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $χL\leftrightarrow\barχΨ$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_χ$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.

2610.37757.title: Seeing Unseen Gravitational Wave Inspirals at the Galactic Center
2610.37757.abstract: The Galactic Center is expected to host a population of extremely large mass-ratio inspirals (X-MRIs) migrating toward the supermassive black hole. We propose an observational approach utilizing the secular gravitational torque exerted by X-MRIs on the highly eccentric S-star S301. This approach is intrinsically limited by the stochastic nature of the surrounding stellar-mass black hole cusp. As S301 propagates through this granular medium, it experiences discrete gravitational encounters. Standard orbital fitting procedures inherently assume a smooth background potential; applying them to stochastic trajectories averages these discrete velocity discontinuities into a continuous secular drift. This introduces a systematic bias that mimics the X-MRI precession signal, invalidating traditional mass estimation techniques. To resolve this degeneracy, we implement a methodology based on the Wavelet Transform Modulus Maxima method to characterize the local Hölder regularity of the orbital motion. This model isolates the singular discontinuities induced by stellar-mass black hole encounters from the continuous torque of the X-MRI distribution, allowing for detection even when instantaneous accelerations are below the instrumental noise threshold. We demonstrate analytically that S301 is highly sensitive to the interior X-MRI population while remaining dynamically decoupled from the secular influence of the exterior cusp. Combining precision astrometry and radial velocity projections, we establish that a minimal population of two X-MRIs is detectable within a five to nine-year timeframe, allowing us to constrain the presence of an unseen orbiter population prior to the launch of space-based gravitational wave detectors.

2610.37214.title: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection
2610.37214.abstract: Coherent emission from merging plasmoids in relativistic reconnection is the leading model for radio emission originating in the outer magnetosphere of pulsars such as the Crab, and a candidate emission mechanism for fast radio bursts. This process has only been studied in 2D, and whether it survives in 3D, where the dynamics of structures in the reconnection layer can differ substantially, is still an open question. Here we present the first study of coherent wave generation from flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection. We use particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields $B_g/B_0 = \{0,0.1,0.3\}$, and measure the efficiency $η$ with which inflowing magnetic energy is converted into escaping coherent waves. We find $η\sim 7\times10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $η\sim(1\text{-}2) \times10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field. We propose a physical picture for why the efficiency remains comparable to 2D, based on how reconnected field is transported away from the diffusion regions. The escaping waves are linearly polarized, with a polarization angle set by the direction of the upstream field. In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the reconnection layer therefore differ in polarization angle by $ \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$. Our results support relativistic magnetic reconnection as the origin of coherent radio emission from Crab-like pulsars, and strengthen its case as a potential emission mechanism for fast radio bursts.

2610.36486.title: Three-flavor neutrino Boltzmann transport and flavor instabilities in long-lived neutron-star merger remnants
2610.36486.abstract: Binary neutron-star (BNS) mergers are multimessenger sources whose kilonova emission and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino microphysics and flavor conversion. Most BNS merger simulations assume $μ$-$τ$ neutrino degeneracy in a two-flavor treatment. We investigate the fast flavor instability (FFI) and the collisional flavor instability (CFI) in long-lived BNS merger remnants using axisymmetric general-relativistic three-flavor Boltzmann neutrino transport with a comprehensive treatment of muons and muonic interactions, following a handoff from 3D grey moment-based simulations. Our simulations largely reproduce the parent 3D simulations, recovering trapped weak equilibrium in the core, muonic non-equilibrium in the semitransparent outer disk due to prolonged demuonization, and cold weak equilibrium in transparent regions. Linear stability analysis reveals strong and widespread CFI in all three flavor sectors, including narrow resonance-like structures. Muonic interactions reshape the FFI distribution, shifting the $eτ$-sector instability toward denser disk regions compared with the extended FFI outside the disk in the two-flavor model, while disk demuonization produces a strong $ν_μ$ excess and one-sided muon-lepton-number angular distributions that suppress FFI in the $eμ$ and $μτ$ sectors. Local three-flavor quantum kinetic equation (QKE) calculations reveal nonlinear coupling among flavor sectors that excites coherence even in an initially stable sector. Diagonal collisional repopulation is decisive for the nonlinear evolution and asymptotic flavor populations, and neglecting it overestimates flavor equilibration. We establish the necessity of three-flavor transport from both classical and quantum perspectives, and underscore the importance of consistently coupling flavor conversion with diagonal collisional repopulation in future CFI subgrid models.

2610.37773.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
2610.37773.abstract: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their hosts stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants as well as chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca ii triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profile characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85-145019.95, a new gas disc system which exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 Rsun to 0.34 Rsun and from 0.54 Rsun to 1.93 Rsun. We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few km to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

2610.37752.title: Disentangling constraints on $S_8$ from the high and low redshift CMB
2610.37752.abstract: The clustering of matter in the universe is quantified by $σ_8$, the RMS fluctuations today in linear theory in spheres of radius $8h^{-1}$ Mpc, where $h$ parametrizes the Hubble constant. Surveys of gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering best constrain $S_8\equiv (Ω_m/0.3)^{0.5} σ_8$, where $Ω_m$ is the energy density of matter in units of the critical density. Comparing this late time measurement to the value of $S_8$ inferred from the cosmic microwave background (CMB), one can test the $Λ$CDM prediction for the growth of clustering from the primordial universe to now. Several analyses report hints that CMB measurements of $S_8$ are larger than those from galaxy surveys. However, CMB measurements have information from both high and low redshift due to lensing, and these tests traditionally conflate the two. Here, we present a technique to extract constraints on the cosmological parameters from each redshift component separately, enabling a high-z vs. low-z clustering comparison that was not previously possible. We marginalize over lensing information using a principal component analysis, and show that the primordial CMB from combined Planck 2018, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 prefers $S_8= 0.795\pm0.022$, in agreement with the recent determination from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) of $S_8=0.789\pm0.012$. The clustering inferred from CMB lensing is larger. However, both the level of excess lensing and increase in agreement with DES depends on the prior on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. We find that removing lensing brings the CMB towards agreement with DES in any case.

2610.38693.title: 2026 ED138: A Large Trans-Neptunian Object in Early Rubin Observatory Data, and How Many More May Remain
2610.38693.abstract: We characterize a large trans-Neptunian object (TNO), 2026 ED138, discovered in data taken by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory with the linking code pointdexter, and validate it independently. 2026 ED138 has absolute magnitude $H_V=3.19$, implying a diameter of 612-1530 km for geometric albedos between 0.25 and 0.04 and making it one of the ten intrinsically brightest known TNOs and a dwarf-planet candidate. At $i\approx19.4$ it is bright enough in the sky for ground-based spectroscopy and light curves and for detailed study with HST and JWST. Archival DECam detections extend its arc to more than ten years (3789 days). Its orbit, with barycentric $a=43.09$ au, $e=0.139$ and $i=24.4^\circ$, lies at the edge of the 12:7 mean-motion resonance with Neptune, like that of the dwarf planet Haumea, but with $g-r=0.63$ it is too red to be a member of Haumea's collisional family. 2026 ED138 was missed by earlier surveys because it lies far south and near the crowded regions of the Galactic plane. Our recoveries of the known TNOs with $H_V<4$ suggest that about 3 more objects like them, and probably more, remain undiscovered away from the Galactic plane. More such objects probably lie within $10^\circ$ of the plane, which no search has yet covered to this depth.

2610.37464.title: How common are extreme scattering events?: First large sample from the ASKAP VAST survey
2610.37464.abstract: Compact radio sources are occasionally observed to undergo extreme scattering events (ESEs): large, chromatic flux-density variations, often by more than a factor of two, over a few months. These were interpreted to be a smooth plasma lensing phenomenon due to AU-scale structures in the ISM. Although ESEs were discovered decades ago, observationally, only a few tens of ESEs have been reported, often from individual sources monitored at very high cadences. As such, the nature of the plasma lenses generating such events remains elusive. In this article, we present the most comprehensive sample of ESEs to date, using the ASKAP Variables and Slow Transients (VAST) survey. We report the discovery of a three-tier sample --- 72 sources that show promising ESE events (gold), 76 sources that are likely ESE-exhibiting (silver), and an additional 88 sources where ESE events are one plausible explanation (bronze). We show that the light curves demonstrate varied morphologies, which can be interpreted in terms of the source size and the strength of the lens in the paradigm of a simple one-dimensional Gaussian lens model. The spatial distribution of ESEs shows an appreciable excess in the direction of the Galactic center and along the Galactic loops. Using this sample, we infer an overall rate of 0.012 such events per year per deg^2 (or 0.006 events per source per year) for our (gold+silver) sample, for sources with mean flux density above 5 mJy at 888 MHz (0.01% of all isolated point sources detected in VAST).

2610.37759.title: Extreme eccentricity in double neutron stars without exotic physics
2610.37759.abstract: The formation of neutron stars (NSs) underpins astrophysical phenomena from supernovae (SNe), radio pulsars and X-ray binaries to double NS mergers that power gravitational waves (GWs), short gamma-ray bursts and r-process kilonovae. A recently reported double NS (PSR J0653+0443) with record eccentricity e=0.9924 provides a unique laboratory for studying GW emission and orbital evolution, and challenges existing formation scenarios. Here we show that such extreme eccentricities arise naturally -- without invoking exotic conditions -- from standard binary-SN physics: instantaneous mass loss (Blaauw recoil) and natal kicks readily produce e>0.99 for both compact and wide pre-SN orbits. The observed orbit matches three families of kinematic solutions spanning a range of kick velocities and progenitor configurations. Physically motivated priors based on NS spin and pre-SN mass transfer constrain the viable progenitor family, demonstrating that the system is not exceptionally rare. Future proper-motion measurements will tightly constrain its natal SN kick magnitude.

2610.38765.title: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
2610.38765.abstract: The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers. Over the years, several methods have been developed to search for this background beyond the standard cross-correlation statistic. We reformulate the data analysis problem for such astrophysical backgrounds in terms of the characteristic function of the data in multiple detectors, and show that the existing searches arise as different limiting cases. We also show that new searches can be constructed through different approximations of the characteristic function, which gives a concrete way to engineer suitable approximate sufficient statistics. To illustrate this framework in the context of a simple example, we use the formalism proposed here to analyze an exactly solvable toy model.

2610.38043.title: Evolutionary Demographics of Molecular Ice Mantles in Young Stars with SPHEREx
2610.38043.abstract: Molecular ices are a primary reservoir of volatile C, O, and N in star-forming environments, tracing the chemical pathway from molecular clouds to planet-forming disks. SPHEREx provides contiguous 0.75--5~$μ$m all-sky spectrophotometry for vastly larger samples than are accessible to JWST, enabling population-scale ice demographics for the first time. We present a search for ice signatures in SPHEREx spectra of 20{,}292 young stellar objects (age $<20$~Myr) drawn from the Gaia-based kinematic catalog of Kounkel \& Covey 2019. Using laboratory templates for the spectral signatures of H$_2$O (3.05~$μ$m), CO$_2$ (4.27~$μ$m), and CO (4.67~$μ$m), we identify 746 H$_2$O ice candidates, including 131 high-confidence H$_2$O+CO$_2$ detections and 22 with additional corroborating CO absorption. When binning by age, we find that the H$_2$O$+$CO$_2$ detection rate declines by an order of magnitude between $\lesssim$3~Myr and $\sim$5~Myr, suggesting a chemical or physical evolutionary trend. Candidates concentrate toward high-extinction sightlines ($A_G \gtrsim 2.5$~mag) and embedded SED morphologies, consistent with the idea of envelope dispersal and photodesorption depleting detectable ice mantles within the first few million years of pre-main-sequence evolution. This catalog provides a homogeneous demographic baseline and a prioritized target list for JWST follow-up.

2610.37044.title: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons
2610.37044.abstract: In energetic astrophysical sources like the gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and blazars, the relativistic electrons lose their energy efficiently through synchrotron radiation and inverse Compton (IC) scattering and can rapidly cool to energies below the minimum acceleration energy $γ_m$. It is widely known that such electrons develop a power-law spectrum $γ_e^{-2}$ below $γ_m$. However, this power-law spectrum is valid only if a steady-state population of electrons is assumed. In general, the cooled electrons below $γ_m$ evolve in a non-steady state and their spectrum deviates significantly from the power-law $γ_e^{-2}$. We present here a new electron spectrum $f_{\rm U}$ that describes this fast-cooled, generally-evolving, and non-steady-state population of electrons below $γ_m$. We consider two cooling cases: (1) when the electrons undergo radiative (i.e., synchrotron + IC) cooling, and (2) when the electrons experience both radiative and adiabatic cooling. We first derive $f_{\rm U}$ analytically and find an explicit expression of $f_{\rm U}$ for each cooling case. Secondly, we show that $f_{\rm U}$ is a solution to a Fokker-Planck equation in the entire energy range below $γ_m$ and derive a general version of $f_{\rm U}$ for each cooling case. We also compare $f_{\rm U}$ to a detailed numerical calculation of a blazar electron spectrum and find an excellent agreement for the whole energy range below $γ_m$. Thus, $f_{\rm U}$ gives us a general electron spectrum to describe the entire cooled electrons below $γ_m$. Our discovery of a new fast-cooling solution $f_{\rm U}$ below $γ_m$ may find it applicable in a wide range of energetic phenomena in high-energy astrophysics.

2610.37414.title: Evidence for a nova super-remnant surrounding the recurrent nova V745 Scorpii using eROSITA
2610.37414.abstract: Nova super-remnants (NSRs) are vast shell-like structures encompassing recurrent novae (RNe), created through the excavation of large amounts of local interstellar medium by repeated nova eruptions. Simulations predict that such NSRs should surround all novae. Indeed, NSRs have now been discovered around the Galactic RNe KT Eridani, RS Ophiuchi and T Coronae Borealis, and the Large Magellanic Cloud RN LMCN 1971-08a, to place alongside the prototypical NSR in M31, associated with the extreme RN, M31N 2008-12a. Highly energetic novae ejecta impacting the inner boundary of the NSR shell alongside inter-ejecta shocks are predicted to generate high levels of X-ray emission in the form of an extended shell-like structure. A search for X-ray emission from a present NSR surrounding the Galactic RN, V745 Scorpii, using observations from the extended Roentgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array (eROSITA) on board Spektrum-Roentgen-Gamma (Spektr-RG, SRG) led to the identification of a shell coincident with the nova. Based on (i) the structure being aligned with the location of the central nova; (ii) its size being consistent with the sizes of other known NSRs; (iii) the similarity between the emission radial profiles of the X-ray structure and the confirmed NSR around M31N 2008-12a; (vi) the presence of a corresponding infrared cavity; (v) the resemblance of the radial profile of the synthetic X-ray ring derived from a modelled NSR structure with the radial profile of the observed ring; and (vi) the lack of other sources capable of creating such a large structure, we propose this X-ray structure to be another Galactic NSR to be uncovered, and the first NSR to be captured through its X-ray emission.

2610.37617.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
2610.37617.abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. Using the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior, we obtain $6.6^{+5.5}_{-2.2}$ expected detections with signal-to-noise ratio $>8$ in 4 years (median and $90\%$ credible interval). The alternative population models we consider use a broken power law with two or three Gaussian peaks for either the primary-mass distribution or a common mass distribution for both black holes. For the three-peak model with the common mass distribution, extrapolating from $300$ to $1000M_\odot$ roughly doubles the median expected number of LISA detections to $\sim14$. The upper end of its $90\%$ credible interval rises from tens to thousands of expected detections, although approximations may limit the reliability of the most extreme counts. For the reference GWTC-5.0 population, $39^{+22}_{-11}\%$ of the binaries detectable by LISA merge during the mission or within $10$ years after its end and are potential multiband sources. Essentially all of these mergers would be detectable by a reference Cosmic Explorer configuration if it is operating at merger. Ground-based measurements of the high-mass population can therefore inform both LISA forecasts and the prospects for observing the same binaries through inspiral and merger.

2610.38956.title: Probing Scalar Polarization with Next-Generation Gravitational-Wave Detectors: The Roles of Detector Geometry and Source Inclination
2610.38956.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. We perform a forecast to assess how well future multi-messenger events will constrain the presence of scalar polarizations in gravitational waves. Performing binary neutron star injections, we forecast next-generation constraints on three modified gravity parameters in the PPE formalism: $α$ (tensor amplitude), $α_B$ (scalar amplitude) and $β$ (tensor and scalar phase). Cosmic Explorer (CE) and Einstein Telescope (ET) each tighten every parameter by 1--2 orders of magnitude over an O5 LIGO-Virgo network, with ET's triangular geometry giving a persistent $\approx2\times$ improvement over 2$\times$CE on the scalar-mode amplitude $α_B$ in both a GW170817-like and a second, representative BNS. We show that, if the sky position and luminosity distance are known from EM observations, adding an EM-based prior on the orbital inclination $ι$ narrows the $α_B$ constraint by $\approx56\times$ relative to an isotropic inclination prior, for a GW170817-like event. We also assess how EM inclination priors as well as assumptions on the neutron star equation of state may affect the inference on the scalar amplitude $α_B$. Overall, these results indicate that detector geometry and the availability of well-placed EM external information are both important levers --- alongside raw network sensitivity --- for next decade scalar-polarization tests.

2610.37942.title: Simulating and Characterizing Non-Gaussian Small-Scale Polarized Emission
2610.37942.abstract: Galactic foregrounds present a major challenge for cosmic microwave background (CMB) cosmology as their amplitudes exceed the target primordial $B$-mode signal. While small-scale interstellar medium (ISM) emission is expected to be highly complex, current foreground simulations cannot reproduce the filamentary, non-Gaussian features of ISM structure in a stochastic way. To address this gap, we introduce a framework for generating stochastic small-scale foreground emission, using polarized synchrotron observations as an example use case. This method is capable of producing many independent realizations that additionally inherit morphological information from large angular scales. The underlying structural complexity incorporates anisotropic, multifractal, and advected non-Gaussian features that are tunable with a small number of parameters that carry physical interpretations. Because standard power spectra do not describe the complex phase coherence required for the structural complexity, we evaluate the synthetic fields using higher-order statistics, demonstrating that the Minkowski functionals and structure functions partially capture varying degrees of non-Gaussianity. This work lays the necessary foundation for new foreground simulation suites with stochastic realizations of possible non-Gaussian structure.

2610.38589.title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
2610.38589.abstract: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

2610.37475.title: Neglecting Dynamical Microlensing Can Bias Accretion Disk Size Measurements at the Population Level
2610.37475.abstract: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars probes unresolved accretion disks, but many inference methods use static magnification maps with fixed relative microlens positions. Using the GPU-accelerated simulator Microcaustics, we generate ten-year multiband light curves for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations. We compare dynamical microlensing with independent microlens motions against coherent bulk motion, and a microlens mass distribution against equal masses, keeping the velocity distribution of individual microlenses and mean mass fixed. We infer population disk sizes using ridge regression on the means and lower and upper scatters of ten variability and event metrics. We measure biases by applying models trained with simplified physics to simulations including both effects. Models trained on coherent motion interpret the additional variability from evolving caustics as smaller disks. For populations of 128 independent realizations, jointly inferred radii are consistently smaller by 6-28%. Microlens dynamics increase caustic-crossing rates pooled across all four macroimages by 5-15% and r-band high-magnification-event (HME) rates by 13-25%, while shortening median HME durations by 4-12%. Omitting the mass distribution produces configuration-dependent disk-size offsets from -12% to +5%. Including the mass distribution decreases caustic-crossing rates by 6-8% and HME rates by 6-12%. It also narrows the spread of ten-year averaged microlensing time-delay differences between macroimages by a median of 9-12% per system, while microlens dynamics have a smaller, image-pair-dependent effect. These results demonstrate the importance of microlens dynamics for population disk-size inference and motivate simulations that include dynamical microlensing and a microlens mass distribution.

2610.37997.title: Search for Eccentric Neutron Star-Black Hole Binaries in Advanced LIGO's Fourth Observing Run using Effective-One-Body Waveforms
2610.37997.abstract: The observation of orbital eccentricity in compact binary coalescences would provide a direct signature of dynamical formation environments. Previous matched-filter searches for eccentric neutron star-black hole (NSBH) binaries have been severely limited by computational constraints, necessitating the use of simplified waveform models that capture secular dephasing but omit apsidal precession and inter-orbit harmonics. Including these physical features increases the sensitive search volume for systems with $0.2 \le e_{20} \le 0.28$ by $\sim 25\%$ to $30\%$. We present a rapid matched-filter search methodology that makes the direct use of time-domain effective-one-body waveforms computationally feasible. By multibanding and high-frequency ratio-filtering, our pipeline achieves a $\sim 20\times$ reduction in computational cost. This allows a bank of 88.6 million effective-one-body templates, fifteen times larger than prior eccentric analyses, to search O4a and O4b Advanced LIGO data. We recover the known low-mass mergers GW230518_125908 and GW230529_181500 with parameters consistent with zero eccentricity. Finding no new gravitational-wave events with orbital eccentricity ($e_{20} \ge 0.05$), we place $90\%$ credible upper limits on the local merger rate density of eccentric NSBH systems across the search space of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 7.5\text{-}57\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, up to a factor of $\sim 4$ improvement over previous observational bounds. At the parameters of GW200105_162426, this non-detection establishes an upper limit of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 12.1\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Alternatively, if GW200105_162426 is treated as an eccentric detection, the lack of subsequent detections in O4 updates the inferred local merger rate density of this population to $\mathcal{R} = 6.6^{+6.3}_{-3.8}\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.

2610.37287.title: The First Deep Learning all-sky List of Fermi-LAT Gamma-ray Sources
2610.37287.abstract: Aims: We develop a deep-learning-based pipeline to construct a list of γ-ray sources and to quantitatively assess the impact of background uncertainties on source detection and characterization. This work extends and enhances the existing AutoSource-ID algorithm, previously adopted on optical observations, for applications on γ-ray data. Methods: Source detection was performed through image segmentation using a U-Net architecture, while dedicated deep neural networks (DNNs) were employed for source localization, flux estimation, and the classification of detected sources as either genuine or spurious. The training data were generated from Monte Carlo simulations based on 10 years of Fermi-LAT observations. Results: We present the first Fermi-LAT γ-ray all-sky source list derived using a deep-learning-based method (1FDL), containing more than 3800 sources with estimated positions, fluxes, and probability scores that quantify the likelihood of each detection being genuine or spurious. We further evaluated the robustness of the pipeline against variations in the interstellar emission model (IEM) and compared the resulting source list with the 4FGL-DR2 catalog. Conclusion: We find that the our deep-learning-based approach achieves performance comparable to, or better than, the likelihood-based methods employed in the standard Fermi-LAT catalog pipeline when tested against changes in the IEM. The 1FDL source list is broadly consistent with the Fermi-LAT 4FGL-DR2 catalog obtained over the same 10-year observational period, including a few new sources confirmed in the recent Fermi-LAT 16-year source list (FL16Y). These results demonstrate the potential of DNN methods for the detection and characterization of γ-ray sources and provide a foundation for their application in future high-energy astrophysical analyses.

2610.37893.title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
2610.37893.abstract: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are among the primary sites of the rapid neutron-capture (r-)process. In mergers with long-lived remnants, sustained neutrino irradiation raises the electron fraction of the disc wind ejecta, modifying the resulting nucleosynthesis pattern. Yields from numerical-relativity simulations with accurate neutrino transport are needed to quantify the contribution of BNS mergers to the Galactic production of heavy elements and to interpret kilonova spectra. We present and publicly release tracer trajectories and nucleosynthesis yields for eight BNS mergers forming long-lived neutron star remnants, obtained from general-relativistic simulations with M1 neutrino transport, spanning two equations of state (DD2 and SFHo), and a range of total masses and mass ratios. Passive tracer particles following the dynamical and wind ejecta were post-processed with the nuclear reaction network WinNet up to 1 Gyr. The yields and tracer trajectories are available on the MARTINI platform. At 1 day, the production of light and first-peak elements (He, Ni, Sr, and Y) is similar across models and is primarily enhanced by the neutrino-irradiated disc wind. The yields of heavy nuclei vary by more than one order of magnitude, with unequal-mass binaries producing the largest amounts owing to their more neutron-rich ejecta. Our He yields, particularly in the wind, exceed those of recent studies based on an M0 neutrino scheme, consistent with the stronger neutrino irradiation resulting from an M1 scheme. At 1 Gyr, all models reproduce the second and third solar r-process peaks, but differ in the first peak, the lanthanide region, the mass range between the first and second peaks, and the trans-lead region, reflecting the electron fraction distribution of the ejecta and the dynamical and wind contributions. Two equal-mass models provide a close match to the solar pattern.

2610.37308.title: Nonradial oscillation modes of axion condensed neutron stars in the Cowling approximation
2610.37308.abstract: In light QCD axion models, finite-density corrections to the axion potential can source a nonvanishing axion field inside neutron stars. Extending our previous analysis of radial oscillations, we study the nonradial ($l=2$) oscillation spectrum of such axion condensed neutron stars in the relativistic Cowling approximation, keeping the fluid and axion perturbations fully coupled and dynamical. The condensate modifies the fluid spectrum in two ways: the altered equilibrium structure raises the $f$- and $p$-mode frequencies by up to $\sim20\%$, while the dynamical coupling to the axion field partially compensates this shift, almost entirely for the $f$-mode. Fluid modes with frequencies above the axion mass acquire a new damping channel through axion emission. The $f$-mode remains below this threshold for all configurations supporting a condensate, whereas the $p$-modes are damped on timescales that can be as short as $\sim10$ ms, shorter than their gravitational-wave damping times, except for certain axion masses where the outgoing axion amplitude nearly vanishes. The spectrum also contains a family of strongly damped axion-dominated quasinormal modes, with imaginary parts of order kHz, and a sequence of gravitationally bound axion states analogous to gravitational atom levels. Below the propagation threshold, the bound $p$-modes undergo avoided crossings with these levels, exchanging their fluid- and axion-dominated character.

2610.37540.title: JWST/MIRI Observations of Amorphous Silicates in Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
2610.37540.abstract: We present JWST/MIRI Low Resolution Spectroscopy (LRS) of 3I/ATLAS obtained post-perihelion at a heliocentric distance of 2.21 au. Our spectrum contains a prominent 10 micron silicate emission feature with a broad, smooth shape that is distinct from those commonly observed in Solar System comets. We model the spectrum using thermal emission from amorphous carbon, amorphous olivine, and amorphous pyroxene grains. Our models strongly favor a pyroxene-dominated, amorphous silicate composition and show a degeneracy between silicate grain size and the relative abundance of silicate and carbon dust. Across a set of representative models, the best-fitting crystalline abundance is zero, and we place an upper limit of 5.3% on the crystalline fraction of the silicates. We identify an emission feature near 6.83 microns that is consistent with aliphatic C-H-bearing material. The overwhelmingly amorphous silicate composition supports previous work that measured unusual volatile and isotopic composition in suggesting that the material incorporated into the object experienced little thermal processing and preserves information about the conditions in which this interstellar planetesimal formed.

2610.36867.title: A microscopic analysis of shear acceleration in the relativistic regime
2610.36867.abstract: Relativistic shear flows, as encountered in jets of powerful astrophysical sources, offer promising sites of particle acceleration up to the highest energies. This stochastic acceleration process is usually described with Fokker-Planck transport equations, which assume small momentum gains per scattering. The present paper introduces a covariant microscopic description of relativistic shear acceleration, building on the formalism of generalized Fermi acceleration and formulating angular scattering in the locally comoving frame in terms of stochastic differential equations. This allows us to model relativistic shear profiles and to study the transition from gradual to non-gradual shear acceleration, where the particle mean free path becomes comparable to the shear length scale. Assuming an infinite shear layer, linear in the flow four-velocity, we observe that the shear rate peaks where the flow is mildly relativistic, whereas Lorentz aberration suppresses the transverse velocity of particles where the flow is relativistic. Consequently, particles that leave the central layer experience long waiting times with a heavy-tailed, power-law distribution. The momentum evolution becomes subdiffusive and the acceleration time can substantially exceed local estimates. We successfully reproduce the Monte Carlo energy distributions using a two-state continuous-time random walk with Lévy-distributed waiting times. We also show how a momentum-dependent mean-free path can introduce breaks in the spectrum and extend our discussion to finite jet profiles. These effects should be accounted for in models of relativistic jets as sources of high-energy particles.

2610.38725.title: Elliptic master integrals and the one-loop cosmological wavefunction
2610.38725.abstract: Loop corrections to the cosmological wavefunction involve similar integrals to those required for scattering amplitudes. For the one-loop triangle of a conformally coupled scalar, the master integrals are elliptic, and so the triangle wavefunction coefficient was expected to be elliptic as well. Using a bootstrap approach, we compute this triangle coefficient exactly and show that it is not: the elliptic periods cancel, and the flat-space wavefunction coefficient is a combination of dilogarithms. The cancellation occurs because the residue of the loop integrand on the elliptic sector is a flat-space amplitude, rational in the loop momentum. The one-loop box, by contrast, is not polylogarithmic, even with a single external leg at each site. Its threshold discontinuity involves elliptic integrals, which we also give in closed form.
